title: Connection Orbits: ephemeral pooling, selective shedding, and graceful stateful failovers
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: During regional surges and downstream latency spikes (Redis/Kafka/primary DB), existing long-lived connection pools cause noisy neighbor effects, slow request queuing, and long tail SLO violations. We lack a lightweight, region-aware connection strategy that lets us: 1) quickly eject bad connections, 2) shed low-value work deterministically, and 3) fail over reads to degraded but available data paths without mass error amplification.

Goal: Implement a new connection orchestration pattern ("Connection Orbits") with ephemeral leased connections, region-aware health scoring, prioritized load shedding, and a controlled degraded-read fallback so that 99th percentile tail latency under dependency pressure improves by 30% and error rate for P99-sensitive routes drops by 60% under simulated downstream degradation.

High-level approach:
- Orbit pools: short-lived leased connections (1-5s) arranged in per-region "orbits" to reduce head-of-line blocking. Pools are coarse-grained per-tenant-class + region + backend-type (redis/kafka/db).
- Lease tokens: callers acquire a token before attempting a network call. Tokens are rate-limited with a bucket per-orbit; tokens expire and automatically release connections to avoid stuck threads.
- Health scoring: connections and orbits receive a rolling health score (latency/failure rate/idle churn). Orbits with degrading score are drifted to a soft-eviction corridor and receive a traffic weight reduction before full circuit open.
- Tiered shedding: requests carry a value score (derived from route config and user tier). During pressure we evict/deny lower-value tokens first (deterministic shedding) and retain high-value traffic lanes.
- Degraded-read fallback: for stateful reads, route to local cache (stale-read mode) or a near-region read-replica. Writes are blocked to degraded paths and receive an explicit 503 + retry-after when necessary.
- Multi-region failover: routing policy shifts client token acquisition to healthy regions using a latency/cost policy; local orbits pre-warm connections to the failover region for quick cutover.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Ephemeral leases increase connection churn and slightly increase CPU overhead; we mitigate via connection reuse windows and pooled transport sockets.
- Stale-read mode increases the chance of serving slightly out-of-date data; limited to low-consistency routes and announced via response metadata.
- Health scoring adds complexity to control plane metrics; we will reuse existing runtime metrics and implement a small scoring function in the proxy to keep rollouts reversible.

Acceptance criteria:
- Integration test harness that simulates Redis/Kafka/DB latency/failure profiles and demonstrates 30% P99 latency improvement for target routes and 60% reduction in P99 error rate under the same injected faults.
- Feature flags for orbit enabled per-tenant and per-route.
- Observability: new metrics (orbit_token_acquire_latency, orbit_health_score, orbit_shed_rate, degraded_read_rate), dashboards, and SLO alerts wired to the on-call runbook.
- Runbook entries for manual failover and rollback; automated canary rollout to 2% then 10% then 50% traffic with automated rollback on error budget burn.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement orbit proxy and token bucket gating behind feature flag (dev env).
2) Canary in staging with chaos tests (fault injection against Redis and DB replicas).
3) Small production canary (2% tenant traffic) with full observability and on-call presence.
4) Gradual ramp with automated health gating and rollback triggers.

Notes on testing and metrics:
- Create a synthetic workload (per-tenant mix) in the load testing cluster that recreates realistic batching patterns for inference requests.
- Track end-to-end SLOs and downstream call-level SLOs separately. Alert when downstream SLOs decrease while end-to-end is stable (indicates effective shielding).

Docs & artifacts: design doc (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Connection+Orbits, PR template and API changes in GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pulls/xyz-orbit-proxy, load test dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/OrbitsLoad/connection-orbits
comments: 2026-03-02 | Ava Martinez: Initial design review completed with runtime and infra. Decided to prototype lease expiry in the proxy rather than the upstream client libs to speed rollout.

2026-03-04 | Marcus Nguyen: Spike implemented for lease token acquisition. Found that short lease TTLs (<=200ms) cause excessive CPU under high QPS—moving to 1s default with adaptive shrink when CPU rises.

2026-03-06 | Priya Shah (SRE): Observability plan reviewed. Added orbit_health_score metric and suggested 5m and 1h rollups for alerts. Also recommended a synthetic canary test that toggles stale-read mode.

2026-03-08 | Design review notes from Lina Gomez (Product): Ensure stale-read mode surfaces X-Redwood-Stale header and opt-out per-tenant. Product requested default shedding to exempt session-affine routes.

2026-03-10 | Marcus Nguyen: Implemented token bucket and soft-eviction corridor. End-to-end tests in CI passing for simulated Redis latency of 200ms median and 1s p99. Next: integrate dashboard panels and start staging canary.
2026-03-10 | QA: Test matrix added to docs: failure modes (redis slow, redis fail, db read-replica lag, kafka leader loss) and expected degraded behaviors.
